text: The bazaar opens quiet as a sealed vial—no scent, no vote, no word from any stall. I trade in what I see, not what I guess, and so far the ledger reads only the names of ten who breathe this air. Hermione, Yoda, Batman, Ripley, Elsa, Morpheus, Inigo, Sherlock, Gandalf—welcome to the morning’s clean page. I will keep this stall open for facts: state a claim, ask a plain question, or hold my tongue. First scent carries farthest—whose nose shall speak first?

Hermione, you are right: the bazaar’s morning ledger shows no claims, no departures, and no role reveals. Gandalf, Yoda, Inigo, Elsa — you each opened with exact counts and still air; that is the shared fact.

So let us trade in those facts: Sherlock, you called for plain trade today. Name a merchant whose words or silence you weigh as evidence. Name the claim or question you carry.

Gandalf, your turn: when you say you listen first, whose voice will you answer when it rises?

Sherlock, you pressed Morpheus to name the concrete quote or action that steered suspicion—yet you yourself have offered none. Hermione demanded evidence and found only silence in the ledger; your call for facts is louder than the facts themselves.

Morpheus accused Gandalf, Yoda, and Inigo of bringing nothing to the table while withholding exactly what he demanded from them. That is a mirrored accusation worth weighing.

Gandalf, Yoda, Inigo—your silence is not guilt; it is the absence of claims against you. The bazaar tests by who speaks, not by who is silent.

Neo measures the silence and finds it exact.

Sherlock, you now state Morpheus “refuses to quote the line that steered suspicion” — yet you still have not quoted the merchant whose words *you* weigh as evidence. Batman, Ripley, Hermione, Neo, Elsa all pressed the same demand, yet none of you have named a single merchant whose own words or silence you treat as proof.

That pattern is louder than the silence: the bazaar’s loudest accusers are the ones who produce no ledger-worthy facts of their own.

Sherlock, the compact rewards plain speech — quote the merchant whose words you lean on tonight.

Sherlock, you state Morpheus “refuses to quote the line that steered suspicion,” yet you still offer no line of your own steering suspicion toward any merchant. Six voices—yourself included—have pressed Morpheus for a concrete quote while producing zero ledger-worthy facts. That mirrored silence is the pattern worth weighing, not the volume.

Morpheus, your accusations of Gandalf, Yoda, and Inigo remain unsupported; cite the exact line or observed act or withdraw them tonight.

The bazaar’s record is unchanged: ten names, zero shutters, zero role reveals.

Sherlock, your call for “the line that steered suspicion” still hangs empty: six voices have now repeated that demand while none of us has named the merchant whose quoted words we lean on. Ripley counted nine demands and found zero lines; Hermione accused Sherlock of withholding evidence yet Hermione, too, cited none. That mirrored silence is the pattern worth weighing, not the volume.

Morpheus, withdraw the unsupported accusation of Gandalf, Yoda, Inigo tonight or cite the exact line that steered it.

Neo: Elsa, your ledger today marks the bazaar’s shared silence—ten names, zero shutters, zero role reveals. Sherlock, Hermione, Ripley, Batman—your calls for “quote the merchant” ring louder than any ledger-worthy quote you’ve produced. Morpheus, your pivot from accusing Gandalf, Yoda, Inigo to demanding evidence still carries the same empty hands. The compact rewards plain speech: name the merchant whose own quoted words you weigh, or admit the absence tonight. The roster does not bend to volume.
